readerContract.humanQuestion: What changed in AI between September 2 and September 9 after last week's launch-heavy roundup, and what do those changes mean for the control I actually have?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: A three-layer map of control: how a reader directs an AI product, how an AI system is bounded, and how law assigns consequences after AI-enabled harm.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: No image-model, agent-evaluation or Take It Down Act background is assumed.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: Control is not one switch. Interface controls shape the request, system boundaries constrain what software may reach, and legal accountability addresses harm after it reaches people.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: A reader may mark one part of an image for revision, decide what an automated tool may access at work, or help someone understand that AI-generated abuse is real abuse with legal routes.
readerContract.surfaceJob: The overdue September 9 Weekly covering September 2–9, prepared transparently on September 10 from current primary-source checks rather than backdated reporting.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I can separate a useful control from a safety boundary or a legal consequence and ask the right question at each layer.
readerContract.desiredReaderFeeling: I understand why better instructions alone do not create a controlled AI system.

canonicalTruth.owner: NewsStand Weekly editor; original sources own the reported facts and current limitations.
canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Recheck each selected primary source and resolve the publication-date mismatch before publisher admission.

strengthsToUse: Make one distinction do useful work across the article
Keep the source limit attached to the claim it limits
End with a precise question the reader can use
patternsNotToCopy: The exact section structure or sentences

glossaryAccumulation.producerGuard: Introduce each term only where it changes the reader's interpretation.
glossaryAccumulation.preventionEvidence: The architecture follows three reported changes and defines system boundaries in context.

templateRepetition.producerGuard: Use one connected argument with proportional sections.
templateRepetition.preventionEvidence: The three items have distinct jobs inside one control-layer thesis.

decorativeAnalogy.producerGuard: Use no analogy unless it maps a mechanism and its limit.
decorativeAnalogy.preventionEvidence: The draft plan uses direct examples and no decorative analogy.

referenceConfetti.producerGuard: Use no Rewind Era reference unless it improves recall of a mechanism.
referenceConfetti.preventionEvidence: No cultural reference is planned for this serious mixed subject.

missingMechanism.producerGuard: Show how direction, permissions and consequences differ link by link.
missingMechanism.preventionEvidence: The causal sequence names the input, reachable environment, action and external harm layers.

genericAction.producerGuard: Give one distinct check for each control layer.
genericAction.preventionEvidence: The planned action asks where instruction ends, what the system can reach and what consequence follows.

jargonBeforeMeaning.producerGuard: Explain the task before naming the technical term.
jargonBeforeMeaning.preventionEvidence: A cyber evaluation is introduced as a controlled test before CTF or monitoring details.

disconnectedSystem.producerGuard: Reconnect each familiar example to the actual product or system boundary.
disconnectedSystem.preventionEvidence: The image mark maps to product input; the work-tool example maps to permissions and network access.

joylessInstruction.producerGuard: Write as an adult newspaper synthesis with pace and point of view.
joylessInstruction.preventionEvidence: The thesis supplies tension without jokes about victims, health or security incidents.

purposeTooNarrow.producerGuard: Serve practical, conceptual and civic understanding together.
purposeTooNarrow.preventionEvidence: The plan connects everyday creation, workplace authority and legal accountability.

mechanismBeforeMotivation.producerGuard: Open with why 'more control' is confusing before technical detail.
mechanismBeforeMotivation.preventionEvidence: The reader question precedes the three-layer mechanism.

workedExampleOvertakesBookPurpose.producerGuard: Keep examples brief and subordinate to the Weekly's evidence map.
workedExampleOvertakesBookPurpose.preventionEvidence: The marked-image and workplace-access cases each clarify one layer only.

technicalExplainerVoice.preventionEvidence: Headlines and planned transitions use ordinary verbs: mark, reach, act and harm.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: The week's three strongest source-complete developments showed that control over AI now has to be judged at three separate layers: the interface, the system boundary and the real-world consequence.
causalSequence: A person gives direction through words, a sketch or a marked edit region
The product and its permissions determine what the system can reach and do
A failure at that boundary can affect real people or systems even when the original task was framed as a test
Law and institutional accountability address some harms after they occur, but do not replace prevention
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A communications manager marks one sleeve for an image edit, then verifies that the rest of the approved composition stayed unchanged.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: A team gives an AI assistant only the shared folders and accounts its task needs, asks for a draft, and keeps sending or publishing behind human approval.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: For a connected AI product, state the task, check the folders, accounts and actions it can use, and keep consequential sending or publishing behind human approval.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Lead with the control distinction; move from user-visible editing to system boundaries and then legal consequence; compare with the prior launch-heavy Weekly; finish with three usable questions.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: The article is one argument supported by three developments, not three equal Daily summaries or a six-item checklist.

humourPlan.noneReason: Security incidents and technology-facilitated sexual abuse require direct, proportionate language; the article can stay lively through clarity and movement.

communicationDesign.surfaceAdaptation: Use a live reader question, make the three control layers concrete through current news, retain vendor and legal limits, and end with a better operational question.

humanQuestion.reason: 'More control' sounds reassuring until the reader asks which layer it describes.
humanQuestion.plannedEvidence: Can I direct the output, bound the system and identify accountability after harm?

usefulCuriosity.reason: The same ordinary word describes three mechanisms that should not be collapsed.
usefulCuriosity.plannedEvidence: A better edit tool can coexist with a failed safety boundary.

invisibleProcessConcrete.reason: The agent incident exposes the hidden path from instruction through permissions to external action.
invisibleProcessConcrete.plannedEvidence: The test said simulation, the environment still reached the internet, and the model kept pursuing the task.

familiarTechnicalMovement.reason: A marked image edit and a bounded work tool make interface and permission layers recognizable.
familiarTechnicalMovement.plannedEvidence: Point to one visual change; separately check which folders, accounts and actions a connected product may use.

limitationsConsequences.reason: Every selected item has a consequential boundary.
limitationsConsequences.plannedEvidence: OpenAI performance claims remain vendor claims; METR is pending; the sentence covered multiple offences.

humourSurprise.reason: Humour would weaken the treatment of cyber incidents and sexual abuse.

betterNextQuestion.reason: The article should change how the reader scopes a real AI task.
betterNextQuestion.plannedEvidence: What can I direct, what can the connected product reach and what approval or reporting route applies if the result reaches someone else?

explanationArc.adaptation: The Weekly answers first, then gives each source-complete development enough mechanism to support the shared distinction.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: A theme about control could flatten three unrelated stories or make a vendor self-assessment sound independently confirmed.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: Bind the exact three primary-source observations, state why the stories are related and how they differ, complete a source-to-claim map and maker read-through, then send the frozen prose to a role-distinct independent reviewer.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: A reader can explain the difference among directing an output, constraining a system and assigning consequences after harm, while naming the unresolved evidence in each story.
